head: 6f0fd72af5f640c243567e9773462a8c90d64c27
boundaries: Actual full ClipboardIslandViewModel, ItemCardViewModel and Core ProjectionCollection execute; no view-model merge or retirement algorithm is copied.
MainViewModel recent-item snapshots and pin results are controlled; RefreshPrimaryQuickActions is a counter-only no-IO signature boundary.
BitmapImage and IStorageItem are identity-only shims; dispatcher scheduling uses explicit queue/completion barriers.
Undo is represented only by a newer revision snapshot, without the production mutation or persistence pipeline.
No real recent-item reads, SQLite, thumbnail/asset IO, native WinUI, XAML binding, UIA or focus behavior is executed; no native focus preservation or IO savings are established.
The retired revision filter checks a card still present when a queued snapshot applies; this is not a persistent tombstone cache.
priorScenarioIntegrity: Default four selection and all four + pin scenario bodies compared byte-for-byte with HEAD before this execution; unchanged.

finalSourceReview.result: No deterministic blocking issue found in the scoped change.
reviewedInvariants: ApplyRecentItems remains inside the original visibility-generation/disposal guard.
Existing same-ID cards are merged through real ItemCardViewModel revision/content contracts; local pending-pin state remains on the retained instance.
Absent accepted IDs are retired before the real Core helper removes them.
Already-retired incoming cards and equal-or-older revisions for retired cards still in the projection are filtered before synchronization.
Newer revisions can restore still-present retired cards through TryMergePresentation, which also retires prior asset generations.
limits: Incoming IDs must be unique, matching the existing recent-item repository contract and shared helper assumptions.
No persistent tombstone remains after an item leaves the collection.
Reordering uses the shared helper Remove/Insert behavior; native focus/container continuity is not established.
Read/thumbnail pipeline and native rendering are unchanged and not executed; no IO savings are claimed.
